A.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones relativas a las cuentas y sus componentes.
A.stem: Una entidad tiene activos de 950 y pasivos de 370. ¿Cuál es su patrimonio?

A.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de transacciones contables en el libro diario.
A.stem: Se compra equipo por 800 al contado, sin impuestos en el caso. ¿Qué asiento corresponde?
A.explanation: Aumenta el equipo y disminuye efectivo, sin alterar patrimonio.
options: Débito a equipo 800 y crédito a caja 800.
Débito a gasto de venta 800 y crédito a ingreso 800.
Débito a caja 800 y crédito a equipo 800.
Débito a equipo 800 y crédito a capital 800.

A.indicatorText: Reconoce las NIIFs usadas en operaciones mercantiles de una empresa de servicios.
A.stem: Una consultora analiza cuándo reconocer ingresos por un contrato con un cliente bajo NIIF completas. ¿Cuál es la referencia principal?
A.explanation: NIIF 15 trata ingresos de contratos con clientes.
options: NIIF 15.
NIC 2 exclusivamente.
NIC 16 exclusivamente.
La política de caja del banco del cliente.

A.indicatorText: Reconoce las NIIFs usadas en operaciones mercantiles de una empresa de servicios.
A.stem: Una firma de diseño compra computadoras para utilizarlas varios años. ¿Qué norma orienta su tratamiento como equipo propio?
A.explanation: Se trata de activos tangibles utilizados en la actividad durante más de un período.
options: NIIF 15 por ser una compra.
NIC 2 por definición en toda computadora.
NIC 16.
Una norma de ingresos agrícolas.

A.indicatorText: Realiza cálculos sobre operaciones con mercancías y el cálculo del impuesto de ventas y la declaración respectiva.
A.stem: Se compran mercancías con base 1000 e IVA del caso de 13 %, totalmente recuperable. ¿Cuánto se carga a inventario?
A.explanation: El IVA recuperable de 130 se separa del costo de mercancías.

A.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de ajuste, relacionados con los ingresos y gastos diferidos y acumulados.
A.stem: Se paga seguro de 1200 por doce meses uniformes y transcurren tres. ¿Qué gasto acumulado debe reconocerse?

A.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de ajuste, relacionados con los ingresos y gastos diferidos y acumulados.
A.stem: Al cierre se deben salarios de 450 ya devengados. ¿Qué ajuste corresponde?
A.explanation: El gasto ocurrió y existe una obligación pendiente.
options: Débito a caja y crédito a ingresos por 450.
Débito a salarios por pagar y crédito a caja por 450.
Débito a gasto de salarios y crédito a salarios por pagar por 450.
No registrar hasta pagar.

A.indicatorText: Describe la importancia del marco conceptual de las NIIFs en las operaciones de una empresa comercial.
A.stem: ¿Qué función cumple el marco conceptual cuando existe una norma específica aplicable?
A.explanation: El marco no prevalece sobre una norma que regula la transacción.
options: Permite ignorarla si la utilidad aumenta.
Elimina toda necesidad de juicio.
Convierte cualquier dato en ingreso.
Ayuda a entenderla, sin reemplazar sus requisitos.

A.indicatorText: Aplica las NIIFs, en las operaciones y estados financieros para una empresa comercial.
A.stem: Mercancías con precio 1000, descuento comercial 100 y flete necesario 50; sin impuestos. ¿Cuál es el costo?

A.indicatorText: Identifica los alcances, etapas, consecuencias y señales de alerta de la legitimación de capitales.
A.stem: ¿Qué describe la legitimación de capitales?
A.explanation: El elemento relevante es la relación con origen delictivo y su ocultación o apariencia de legitimidad.
options: Toda ganancia obtenida por una empresa.
Cualquier compra internacional legal.
El pago puntual de un impuesto.
Ocultar o dar apariencia lícita a bienes de origen delictivo.

A.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones relativas a la legitimación de capitales.
A.stem: Una empresa recibe fondos de un tercero desconocido para cancelar una factura ajena. ¿Qué corresponde inicialmente?
A.explanation: La incongruencia exige análisis y documentación, no presunciones definitivas.
options: Verificar relación, propósito y soporte conforme al procedimiento.
Registrar una venta adicional ficticia.
Declarar públicamente culpable al tercero.
Omitir revisión porque el dinero llegó.

A.indicatorText: Contrasta las obligaciones de patronos y trabajadores ante la Caja Costarricense del Seguro Social (C.C.S.S). y el Código de Trabajo.
A.stem: Una empresa descuenta del salario una cuota autorizada para seguridad social. ¿Qué debe hacer con ese importe?
A.explanation: La retención origina una obligación, no un recurso propio disponible sin destino.
options: Reconocerlo como ingreso por ventas.
Entregarlo al gerente como gratificación.
Enterarlo a la entidad correspondiente según el procedimiento aplicable.
Eliminar el pasivo sin pagar.

A.indicatorText: Contrasta las obligaciones de patronos y trabajadores ante la Caja Costarricense del Seguro Social (C.C.S.S). y el Código de Trabajo.
A.stem: ¿Cuál es una obligación de la persona trabajadora?
A.explanation: El deber de colaboración no incluye cumplir órdenes ilícitas.
options: Pagar siempre la contribución propia del patrono.
Renunciar por escrito a toda seguridad social.
Alterar planillas si se lo ordenan.
Seguir instrucciones legítimas y medidas de seguridad del trabajo.

A.indicatorText: Reconoce lo referente la normativa del Impuesto sobre las Ventas y el Impuesto sobre Bienes Muebles.
A.stem: ¿Qué distinción es correcta al estudiar tributos?
A.explanation: La obligación depende del hecho imponible y de su norma.
options: Poseer y vender son siempre el mismo hecho.
Vender un bien y poseerlo pueden constituir hechos gravados diferentes.
Todo tributo sobre bienes se calcula como IVA.
Todo cargo de un recibo tiene la misma base.

A.indicatorText: Calcula la resolución de situaciones que involucren el cálculo y registro del impuesto sobre ventas y el Impuesto sobre Bienes Muebles.
A.stem: Una venta tiene base 8000 y tarifa IVA del caso de 13 %. ¿Cuál es el total facturado?

A.indicatorText: Recognize appropriate habits to work with computers.
A.stem: An accountant leans forward to read tiny figures. What should be tried first?
A.explanation: The arrangement should support the task instead of forcing an awkward posture.
options: Keep leaning for the whole shift.
Place the screen farther away without checking readability.
Ignore the problem because spreadsheets require it.
Improve text size and screen arrangement for comfortable reading.

A.indicatorText: Apply hygiene and security habits when using a computer.
A.stem: A payroll clerk leaves the desk for a meeting. What should happen to the active session?
A.explanation: Locking reduces unauthorized access during the absence.
options: It should be locked before leaving.
It should remain open for any passerby.
The password should be written beside the keyboard.
The payroll file should be copied to a public folder.

A.indicatorText: Define the concept and characteristic of viruses.
A.stem: Malicious code is inserted into executable files and runs with the infected file. Which category best describes that replication mechanism?
A.explanation: The host-file dependency identifies the virus mechanism.
options: A worm spreading without a host file.
Adware identified only by advertising behavior.
A denial-of-service traffic flood.
A computer virus.

A.indicatorText: Differentiate characteristics of different anti virus.
A.stem: Which feature checks suspicious activity while files are used?
A.explanation: Real-time monitoring operates during activity rather than only on request.
options: An on-demand scan run only when requested.
A weekly inventory of installed programs.
Real-time protection.
A one-time scan before software installation.

A.indicatorText: Distinguishes characteristics, functions and services for different devices.
A.stem: Which device normally forwards packets between an office network and another network?
A.explanation: Routing connects different networks and selects packet forwarding paths.
options: A router.
A basic Layer 2 switch with no routing function.
A passive Ethernet patch panel.
A wireless adapter acting only as a client.

A.indicatorText: Distinguishes characteristics, functions and services for different devices.
A.stem: A laptop shows a Wi-Fi connection but cannot reach an Internet site. What is possible?
A.explanation: Local connectivity does not guarantee all upstream services.
options: The local wireless link works while the Internet connection or remote service fails.
Wi-Fi always proves that every Internet service is available.
The laptop must have no network adapter.
A successful Wi-Fi link eliminates DNS problems.

A.indicatorText: Differentiates the new theories used to manage the modern organizations.
A.stem: A team measures invoice errors, tests a small change and checks whether errors fall. Which approach is most evident?
A.explanation: The team learns through measured incremental changes.
options: A complete replacement of the business model by definition.
Outsourcing of all accounting.
Elimination of all process measurement.
Continuous improvement.

A.indicatorText: Differentiates the new theories used to manage the modern organizations.
A.stem: A company replaces a six-stage approval process with a fundamentally redesigned workflow. Which approach best fits?
A.explanation: The main change is structural redesign of the process.
options: Routine end-of-day filing.
A minor spelling correction.
A customer satisfaction survey alone.
Business process reengineering.

A.indicatorText: Defines marketing.
A.stem: Which statement best describes marketing?
A.explanation: Marketing includes activities before, during and after a transaction.
options: Understanding markets and creating, communicating and delivering valuable offerings.
Only collecting cash after a sale.
Only designing advertisements.
Only reducing every price to the minimum.

A.indicatorText: Recognizes variables of mixed market.
A.stem: A company adds a repair warranty to its offering. Which P is most directly affected?
A.explanation: The warranty changes the benefits and support included in the offering.
options: Product.
Place only.
Promotion only.
Price only.

A.indicatorText: Describes the behavior of a professional at the table, as a host, or guest in a restaurant or at home.
A.stem: A host needs to know whether guests have dietary requirements. What is the appropriate approach?
A.explanation: Advance, discreet coordination respects privacy and participation.
options: Require public explanations at the table.
Ask discreetly in advance and coordinate suitable options.
Assume everyone eats the same food.
Pressure guests to accept the selected dish.

A.indicatorText: Defines compound interest components.
A.stem: In F = P(1+i)^n, what does P represent?
A.explanation: P is the amount invested or financed at the start.
options: The interest earned only.
The number of compounding periods.
The initial principal.
The future amount after interest.

A.indicatorText: Calculates compound interest.
A.stem: Invest 1000 at 10% effective annually for two years, with no other cash flows. What is the future amount?
A.explanation: 1000×1.10² = 1210; the second year earns interest on 1100.

A.indicatorText: Calculates factoring in managerial financing means.
A.stem: Receivables of 10000 are factored with a fee of 3% of face value. What is the fee?

A.indicatorText: Lists the concept and importance of accounts payable.
A.stem: What does a trade account payable normally represent?
A.explanation: Payables and receivables represent opposite sides of the credit relationship.
options: A customer’s advance for an unperformed service.
The owner’s permanent capital contribution.
Cash that a customer still owes the business.
An obligation to a supplier for goods or services received on credit.

A.indicatorText: Solves payable accounts transactions in foreign currencies and operations shown in financial statements with corresponding footnotes.
A.stem: Functional currency is CRC. A payable of USD 2000 is first recognized at CRC 500 per USD. What is its initial amount?

A.indicatorText: Mentions about inventories according to company’s nature (activity).
A.stem: A clothing retailer buys shirts to sell without manufacturing them. What are those shirts?
A.explanation: They are goods held for resale.
options: The retailer’s production machinery.
Accounts payable by themselves.
Prepaid advertising.
Merchandise inventory.

A.indicatorText: Determines reasons for adjusting entries.
A.stem: The ledger shows 100 units at 8 each; a verified shortage of 5 units requires adjustment under the case. What amount is removed from inventory?
A.explanation: 5×8 = 40; the remaining 95 units have cost 760 before other adjustments.

A.indicatorText: Recognizes importance of property term, place and equipment.
A.stem: Which item is normally property, plant and equipment for a bakery?
A.explanation: The oven is a tangible operating asset used over several periods.
options: Bread held for sale tomorrow.
Flour awaiting production.
A customer’s unpaid invoice.
An oven used to bake products for several years.

A.indicatorText: Answers cases of property, place and equipment and its presentation in the general balance.
A.stem: A machine costs 20000; necessary transport is 1000 and installation 2000. Training costs 500. No taxes apply. What initial machine cost is used in the case?
A.explanation: Purchase, transport and installation total 23000; training is not included in this asset cost.

A.indicatorText: Names accounts that make the patrimony.
A.stem: Which account normally forms part of equity?
A.explanation: Retained earnings accumulate undistributed results and related changes.
options: Retained earnings.
Trade accounts payable.
Bank loan principal.
Wages payable.

A.indicatorText: Classifies patrimony accounts.
A.stem: Beginning equity is 500, contributions 100, profit 80 and distributions 30, with no other changes. What is ending equity?

A.indicatorText: Mentions aspects about the savings and loan associations.
A.stem: An association lends 1000 to a member. What does the association normally recognize for the principal?
A.explanation: The association has a claim for repayment rather than income from the principal itself.
options: Revenue of 1000 simply for lending.
A loan receivable.
A reduction in all member savings automatically.
An operating expense equal to the principal.

A.indicatorText: Names objectives of the working capital analysis and statement of change in the financial position based on cash.
A.stem: Current assets are 900 and current liabilities 540. What is net working capital?
A.explanation: 900−540 = 360. The amount is different from the current ratio.

A.indicatorText: Enumerates the financial control of the working capital.
A.stem: Which report helps identify overdue customer balances?
A.explanation: Aging groups receivables by time outstanding or due status.
options: A fixed-asset depreciation table.
A list of office furniture colors.
An accounts receivable aging schedule.
A schedule of owner birthdays.

A.indicatorText: Lists objectives and importance of both statements for the companies.
A.stem: A company pays a current payable of 100 using cash. What happens to net working capital, with no other effects?
A.explanation: The difference between the two current totals is unchanged.
options: It rises by 100.
It falls by 100.
It becomes equal to total equity.
It stays unchanged because current assets and current liabilities both fall by 100.

A.indicatorText: Applies methods to develop the analysis of the working capital and statements of change in the financial position based on the working capital.
A.stem: Beginning current assets are 700 and current liabilities 400; ending amounts are 850 and 450. What is the increase in net working capital?
A.explanation: Beginning 300; ending 400; increase 100.

A.indicatorText: Recognizes the tools used to carry out financial analysis statements.
A.stem: Sales increase from 400 to 500. What is the percentage increase?
A.explanation: (500−400)÷400×100 = 25%; the earlier amount is the base.

A.indicatorText: Interprets the results obtained from the financial ratios.
A.stem: Current assets are 600 and current liabilities 300. What is the current ratio?
options: 0.5 times.
300 times.
3 times.
2 times.

A.indicatorText: Recognizes concept of leaders, types of leaders and functions of leaders.
A.stem: Which action illustrates leadership rather than only holding a title?
A.explanation: Leadership supports coordinated progress toward a purpose.
options: Refusing to explain priorities.
Clarifying the goal and helping the team remove a work obstacle.
Assuming authority guarantees trust.
Measuring only time spent at the desk.

A.indicatorText: Recognizes the importance of administrative inventory systems in a company as in delay time, line, locations, suppliers and storage of raw material.
A.stem: Daily demand is 20 units, lead time five days and safety stock 30 units. What is the reorder point under the stated model?
options: 100 units.
50 units.
130 units.
600 units.

A.indicatorText: Recognizes the importance of administrative inventory systems in a company as in delay time, line, locations, suppliers and storage of raw material.
A.stem: What does supplier lead time describe in a replenishment case?
A.explanation: Lead time is a time interval affecting replenishment planning.
options: The number of units sold per day.
The unit selling price.
The time between placing an order and the goods becoming available as defined.
The age of the warehouse building.

A.indicatorText: Adequately calculates rates for each element of cost using bases.
A.stem: A product requires 3 kg of material at 4 per kg. What is its standard direct material cost?

A.indicatorText: Adequately calculates rates for each element of cost using bases.
A.stem: Standard labor time is 1.5 hours per unit and the rate is 8 per hour. What is standard direct labor cost?

A.indicatorText: Distinguishes introductory concepts of costs for continuous or departmental process.
A.stem: Which operation is most suited to process costing?
A.explanation: Process costing fits repeated, similar production accumulated by process.
options: A single custom building contract with separately traced costs.
Unrelated consulting projects billed individually.
Continuous production of many similar units through the same stages.
A unique repair job for each customer.

A.indicatorText: Summarizes costs.
A.stem: Manufacturing costs are materials 8000, direct labor 7000 and overhead 5000. What is total manufacturing cost added?

A.indicatorText: Comments about countable field processes of combined products, by-products and co-products.
A.stem: What is the split-off point?
A.explanation: Before split-off, costs belong to the common process.
options: The date every customer pays.
The point where outputs of a joint process become separately identifiable.
The point where all products have equal prices.
The moment all inventory is sold.

A.indicatorText: Applies methods to assign combined costs.
A.stem: Joint cost is 5000. Outputs are A 300 kg and B 200 kg. Using physical quantities, what is allocated to A?

A.indicatorText: Differs among physical and mental load.
A.stem: Holding the neck in one position for a long period is mainly an example of which demand?
A.explanation: Sustained posture is a physical exposure even without heavy lifting.
options: Only a financial reporting demand.
A physical postural demand.
A demand that disappears because the worker is seated.
Only the complexity of a tax rule.

A.indicatorText: Describes consequences of physical and mental workload on people and productivity.
A.stem: Errors rise near the end of repeated long closing shifts. What is a sound response?
A.explanation: The pattern is evidence for investigation, not a complete explanation by itself.
options: Assume every worker is careless without review.
Hide corrections to preserve the performance metric.
Remove all breaks to regain lost time.
Investigate workload, scheduling and process conditions.

A.indicatorText: Identifies principles that regulate the auditor.
A.stem: An auditor is asked to omit a known error to keep the client satisfied. Which principle most directly calls for honesty in the response?
A.explanation: Integrity requires honest conduct rather than deliberate misrepresentation.
options: A requirement to maximize the client’s reported profit.
An exemption from evidence gathering.
A rule that client approval replaces professional judgment.
Integrity.

A.indicatorText: Determines the means to achieve the internal control in corporate accounts.
A.stem: What level of assurance is generally associated with internal control?
A.explanation: Human error, collusion and other limitations prevent absolute assurance.
options: Absolute certainty that no error can occur.
A guarantee of profitability.
No assurance because procedures are documented.
Reasonable assurance, with inherent limitations.

A.indicatorText: Interprets situations concerning the means to achieve a better internal control of the accounts of the company.
A.stem: The cashier also prepares and approves the bank reconciliation without review. What improvement is most relevant?
A.explanation: An independent check can detect errors or concealment that self-review may miss.
options: Changing the reconciliation’s font.
Removing bank statements from the process.
Independent review of the reconciliation and supporting evidence.
Requiring the cashier to approve twice.

A.indicatorText: Mentions the projected profit and loss statement also the objectives of the projected profit and loss statement.
A.stem: Projected sales are 10000, cost of sales 6000 and operating expenses 2500. With no other items, what is projected profit?

A.indicatorText: Determines methods to project sales.
A.stem: Sales in the last three comparable months were 100, 120 and 140 units. What is the three-month simple moving-average forecast?
options: 140 units.
360 units.
110 units.
120 units.

B.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones relativas a las cuentas y sus componentes.
B.stem: Caja registra débitos por 700 y créditos por 250, sin saldo inicial. ¿Qué saldo presenta?
B.explanation: Una cuenta de activo queda deudora cuando sus débitos superan los créditos.
options: Saldo deudor de 450.
Saldo acreedor de 450.
Saldo deudor de 950.
Saldo acreedor de 250.

B.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de transacciones contables en el libro diario.
B.stem: Se cobran 300 de una cuenta por cobrar ya registrada. ¿Qué asiento corresponde?
B.explanation: Se transforma un activo en otro; no se repite la venta.
options: Débito a caja 300 y crédito a cuentas por cobrar 300.
Débito a caja 300 y crédito a ventas 300.
Débito a cuentas por pagar 300 y crédito a caja 300.
Débito a gastos 300 y crédito a caja 300.

B.indicatorText: Reconoce las NIIFs usadas en operaciones mercantiles de una empresa de servicios.
B.stem: Un cliente paga antes de que se preste el servicio contratado. ¿Qué debe evitarse?
B.explanation: El ingreso depende del cumplimiento pertinente, no solo del cobro.
options: Identificar la obligación pendiente.
Reconocer automáticamente todo como ingreso ganado al cobrar.
Conservar el contrato.
Registrar el efectivo recibido.

B.indicatorText: Reconoce las NIIFs usadas en operaciones mercantiles de una empresa de servicios.
B.stem: ¿Qué norma se consulta para estudiar provisiones y pasivos contingentes?
B.explanation: NIC 37 diferencia obligaciones y contingencias bajo sus condiciones.
options: NIC 16.
NIC 37.
NIC 2.
NIC 7 como única norma de reconocimiento.

B.indicatorText: Realiza cálculos sobre operaciones con mercancías y el cálculo del impuesto de ventas y la declaración respectiva.
B.stem: Una venta tiene precio final 2260, incluido IVA del 13 %. ¿Cuál es la base?

B.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de ajuste, relacionados con los ingresos y gastos diferidos y acumulados.
B.stem: Se recibieron 900 por un servicio de tres meses que se cumple uniformemente. Al cierre ha transcurrido un mes. ¿Cuánto ingreso se reconoce?
B.explanation: Se ganó un tercio del servicio: 900÷3.

B.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de ajuste, relacionados con los ingresos y gastos diferidos y acumulados.
B.stem: Se prestó un servicio de 700 aún no facturado; el caso indica que ya cumple requisitos de ingreso y cobro incondicional. ¿Qué se registra?
B.explanation: Existe ingreso devengado y derecho de cobro bajo las condiciones dadas.
options: Cuenta por cobrar e ingreso por 700.
Solo una entrada a caja por 700.
Un anticipo de clientes por 700.
Una disminución del patrimonio por 700.

B.indicatorText: Describe la importancia del marco conceptual de las NIIFs en las operaciones de una empresa comercial.
B.stem: ¿Qué cualidades fundamentales se asocian con información financiera útil?
B.explanation: Las cifras deben importar para decisiones y representar el hecho adecuadamente.
options: Popularidad y publicidad.
Relevancia y representación fiel.
Velocidad y tamaño del archivo.
Secreto y ausencia de estimaciones.

B.indicatorText: Aplica las NIIFs, en las operaciones y estados financieros para una empresa comercial.
B.stem: Se vende por 800 una mercancía cuyo importe registrado es 500, sin otros gastos ni impuestos. ¿Cuál es la utilidad bruta?
B.explanation: Ingreso 800 menos costo de venta 500 = 300.

B.indicatorText: Identifica los alcances, etapas, consecuencias y señales de alerta de la legitimación de capitales.
B.stem: ¿Qué conjunto corresponde al modelo de etapas usado para estudiar lavado de activos?
B.explanation: Son categorías analíticas; no siempre se observan como etapas rígidas y separadas.
options: Colocación, estratificación e integración.
Compra, almacenamiento y reparto como definición suficiente.
Planificación, licitación y adjudicación.
Activo, pasivo y patrimonio.

B.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones relativas a la legitimación de capitales.
B.stem: ¿Cuál afirmación distingue una alerta de una prueba?
B.explanation: El juicio debe basarse en evidencia y competencias correspondientes.
options: Toda alerta equivale a condena.
Solo hay alerta cuando existe sentencia.
Una alerta obliga a borrar el asiento.
La alerta motiva evaluación; no demuestra por sí sola un delito.

B.indicatorText: Contrasta las obligaciones de patronos y trabajadores ante la Caja Costarricense del Seguro Social (C.C.S.S). y el Código de Trabajo.
B.stem: El patrono propone reportar solo la mitad del salario real. ¿Qué corresponde?
B.explanation: El reporte debe representar la remuneración que corresponde declarar.
options: Aceptar porque reduce cualquier obligación legal.
Mantener información veraz y corregir el reporte según el procedimiento.
Borrar el contrato y continuar igual.
Registrar la otra mitad como ingreso de la empresa.

B.indicatorText: Contrasta las obligaciones de patronos y trabajadores ante la Caja Costarricense del Seguro Social (C.C.S.S). y el Código de Trabajo.
B.stem: ¿Qué diferencia debe preservarse en una planilla?
B.explanation: Las obligaciones tienen responsables y tratamientos distintos.
options: Todos los cargos son siempre del trabajador.
Aportes a cargo del patrono y deducciones autorizadas a cargo del trabajador.
Todas las retenciones son ventas.
Aseguramiento y pago de salario son lo mismo.

B.indicatorText: Reconoce lo referente la normativa del Impuesto sobre las Ventas y el Impuesto sobre Bienes Muebles.
B.stem: Un vehículo y un terreno aparecen en el registro de activos. ¿Qué debe evitarse al calcular sus tributos?
B.explanation: La clasificación contable como activo no iguala su régimen tributario.
options: Identificar la naturaleza de cada bien.
Revisar la norma específica.
Aplicarles automáticamente la misma norma por ser ambos activos.
Comprobar base y período.

B.indicatorText: Calcula la resolución de situaciones que involucren el cálculo y registro del impuesto sobre ventas y el Impuesto sobre Bienes Muebles.
B.stem: Un ejercicio de propiedad inmobiliaria da base fiscal 20000000 y tarifa anual supuesta de 0,25 %. ¿Cuál es el tributo anual?
B.explanation: 20000000×0,0025 = 50000. Se usa la regla suministrada.

B.indicatorText: Recognize appropriate habits to work with computers.
B.stem: Which habit helps during prolonged computer work?
B.explanation: Recovery and variation reduce continuous exposure to the same demands.
options: Remain in exactly one posture all day.
Replace every break with intensive phone use.
Skip all pauses until the report is finished.
Vary tasks and take suitable short breaks.

B.indicatorText: Apply hygiene and security habits when using a computer.
B.stem: How should a computer be cleaned?
B.explanation: Cleaning must avoid electrical and equipment damage.
options: Spray liquid directly into the keyboard and ports.
Open a powered electrical supply without training.
Follow the manufacturer’s instructions and keep liquids out of openings.
Block all vents to prevent dust.

B.indicatorText: Define the concept and characteristic of viruses.
B.stem: What distinguishes a worm from the virus mechanism described in basic classifications?
B.explanation: Independent propagation is the key distinction, not the name of the affected application.
options: A worm can propagate independently without attaching to a host file.
A worm is always harmless.
A worm can only exist on paper.
A worm must be a spreadsheet formula.

B.indicatorText: Differentiate characteristics of different anti virus.
B.stem: A harmless accounting utility is flagged as malicious. What is this called?
B.explanation: The alert is positive while the object is not malicious.
options: A false negative.
A false positive.
A confirmed infection by definition.
A successful backup.

B.indicatorText: Distinguishes characteristics, functions and services for different devices.
B.stem: Which technology commonly connects a nearby wireless mouse to a laptop?
B.explanation: Bluetooth supports short-range peripheral connections.
options: Cellular roaming.
A wired Ethernet uplink.
Satellite Internet access.
Bluetooth.

B.indicatorText: Distinguishes characteristics, functions and services for different devices.
B.stem: What is the usual function of a wireless access point?
B.explanation: It supplies wireless network access; other functions may be separate.
options: Assign a public address to every Internet website.
Translate every file into a wireless-only format.
Guarantee Internet service independently of any upstream link.
Provide compatible wireless devices access to the local network.

B.indicatorText: Differentiates the new theories used to manage the modern organizations.
B.stem: An organization compares its order-processing practice with a strong reference organization and studies the gap. What is it doing?
B.explanation: Benchmarking uses comparisons to identify learning opportunities.
options: Benchmarking.
Recording depreciation.
Delegating ownership of the whole company.
Assuming that all organizations are identical.

B.indicatorText: Differentiates the new theories used to manage the modern organizations.
B.stem: What is necessary for meaningful empowerment?
B.explanation: People need the means and scope to act responsibly.
options: Defined authority supported by information, skills and boundaries.
Responsibility without any access or authority.
Unlimited decisions without accountability.
Removing all training because staff are trusted.

B.indicatorText: Defines marketing.
B.stem: A customer pays more for reliable delivery that avoids production delays. What does this illustrate?
B.explanation: The customer evaluates the benefit in the context of their needs.
options: Price never matters.
Every customer values the same feature equally.
Value can include benefits beyond a low purchase price.
Delivery is unrelated to the offering.

B.indicatorText: Recognizes variables of mixed market.
B.stem: A business starts selling through an authorized online distributor. Which P describes the channel decision?
B.explanation: Place concerns how the offering reaches customers.
options: Product formulation.
Place.
Price calculation only.
Promotion message only.

B.indicatorText: Describes the behavior of a professional at the table, as a host, or guest in a restaurant or at home.
B.stem: A guest does not drink alcohol. What should the host do?
B.explanation: Professional courtesy does not depend on alcohol consumption.
options: Insist that drinking proves commitment.
Ask the group to persuade the guest.
Cancel the business conversation immediately.
Respect the choice and offer an appropriate alternative.

B.indicatorText: Defines compound interest components.
B.stem: A nominal annual rate of 12% is compounded monthly. What periodic rate is used under that quotation?
B.explanation: The nominal rate is divided by twelve compounding periods.
options: 12% per month.
0.12% per month.
An effective annual rate of exactly 12% in all cases.
1% per month.

B.indicatorText: Calculates compound interest.
B.stem: A future target is 2420 after two years at 10% effective annually. What principal is needed today?

B.indicatorText: Calculates factoring in managerial financing means.
B.stem: A factor pays face value 20000 less a fee of 400 and a refundable holdback of 2000. What cash is received immediately?
B.explanation: Immediate cash = 20000−400−2000; the holdback is not cash received now.

B.indicatorText: Lists the concept and importance of accounts payable.
B.stem: Why is a supplier aging schedule useful?
B.explanation: Due information supports planning but does not replace validity checks.
options: It shows when obligations are due or overdue.
It proves that every invoice was authorized.
It replaces all receipt documents.
It guarantees enough cash for every payment.

B.indicatorText: Solves payable accounts transactions in foreign currencies and operations shown in financial statements with corresponding footnotes.
B.stem: A USD 2000 payable has a carrying amount of CRC 1000000. At closing, the rate is CRC 520 per USD. What difference arises in this ordinary case?
B.explanation: The liability increases to 1040000; the increase is a loss.
options: An exchange gain of CRC 40000.
No difference because the dollar amount is unchanged.
An exchange loss of CRC 40000.
An exchange loss of CRC 1040000.

B.indicatorText: Mentions about inventories according to company’s nature (activity).
B.stem: A manufacturer has partly assembled products that still require processing. How are they classified?
B.explanation: Production has begun but the goods are not yet complete.
options: Finished goods ready for sale.
Office equipment.
Work in process.
Customer deposits.

B.indicatorText: Determines reasons for adjusting entries.
B.stem: All units are present, but their cost exceeds net realizable value. Can an adjustment still be needed?
B.explanation: Quantity and measurement are separate aspects of inventory.
options: No, a count proves every valuation is correct.
Yes, physical accuracy does not ensure recoverable value.
Only if the supplier changes its name.
Only if the inventory is sold for cash first.

B.indicatorText: Recognizes importance of property term, place and equipment.
B.stem: What is the main purpose of depreciation?
B.explanation: Depreciation is an allocation process, not a cash transfer or market appraisal.
options: Guarantee the asset’s sale price.
Set aside cash automatically in a bank account.
Allocate the depreciable amount over useful life using an appropriate pattern.
Record a supplier payment every month.

B.indicatorText: Answers cases of property, place and equipment and its presentation in the general balance.
B.stem: Equipment costs 12000, residual value is 2000 and useful life is five years. What is annual straight-line depreciation for a full year?

B.indicatorText: Names accounts that make the patrimony.
B.stem: An owner makes an ordinary permanent capital contribution. How is it distinguished from a sale?
B.explanation: The owner acts as owner, not as a customer buying the entity’s output.
options: It always creates sales revenue.
It is always an unpaid supplier invoice.
It increases contributed equity rather than customer revenue.
It has no effect on assets or equity.

B.indicatorText: Classifies patrimony accounts.
B.stem: A transfer of 40 moves retained earnings into an equity reserve, with no other effect. How does total equity change?
B.explanation: The transfer reallocates amounts within equity.
options: It increases by 40.
It decreases by 40.
It doubles.
It does not change.

B.indicatorText: Mentions aspects about the savings and loan associations.
B.stem: A member’s stated monthly saving is 4% of a salary of 600000. What amount is saved under the case?
B.explanation: 600000×0.04 = 24000; the percentage is supplied for the exercise.

B.indicatorText: Names objectives of the working capital analysis and statement of change in the financial position based on cash.
B.stem: What is a main purpose of the statement of cash flows?
B.explanation: It organizes cash movements and their sources and uses.
options: Explain changes in cash and cash equivalents during the period.
List only unpaid supplier invoices.
Replace all income-statement information.
Guarantee future profitability.

B.indicatorText: Enumerates the financial control of the working capital.
B.stem: Why should obsolete stock be separated from usable stock in liquidity analysis?
B.explanation: Recorded quantity can overstate practical availability or recovery.
options: It always has a higher cash value.
It may not convert into expected cash through normal sales.
Its physical presence proves full recoverability.
It automatically pays suppliers.

B.indicatorText: Lists objectives and importance of both statements for the companies.
B.stem: Which statement distinguishes the two analytical bases?
B.explanation: Net working capital includes noncash current assets and current liabilities.
options: Both always equal net profit.
Cash and net working capital are different measures of funds.
Working capital includes only banknotes.
Cash flow ignores every financing transaction.

B.indicatorText: Applies methods to develop the analysis of the working capital and statements of change in the financial position based on the working capital.
B.stem: A simplified reconciliation starts from profit 500, adds depreciation 80 and subtracts an increase in receivables of 60. No other adjustments apply. What is operating cash flow?

B.indicatorText: Recognizes the tools used to carry out financial analysis statements.
B.stem: In a common-size income statement using sales as 100%, expenses are 60 and sales are 200. What percentage represents those expenses?

B.indicatorText: Interprets the results obtained from the financial ratios.
B.stem: Net profit is 90 and sales are 1500. What is net profit margin?

B.indicatorText: Recognizes concept of leaders, types of leaders and functions of leaders.
B.stem: A manager invites staff to analyze options before choosing a workflow. Which approach is most evident?
B.explanation: The team contributes to the decision process.
options: Fully unilateral direction without consultation.
Delegation with no shared discussion.
Avoidance of every management decision.
Participative leadership.

B.indicatorText: Recognizes the importance of administrative inventory systems in a company as in delay time, line, locations, suppliers and storage of raw material.
B.stem: On-hand stock is 80, outstanding orders 50 and backorders 20. What is inventory position under the stated definition?
options: 150 units.
60 units.
130 units.
110 units.

B.indicatorText: Recognizes the importance of administrative inventory systems in a company as in delay time, line, locations, suppliers and storage of raw material.
B.stem: Why record storage locations for materials?
B.explanation: Location records support retrieval and traceability.
options: So quantity counts are no longer necessary.
So every item has the same expiry date.
So supplier delivery time becomes zero.
So required stock can be found and controlled when needed.

B.indicatorText: Adequately calculates rates for each element of cost using bases.
B.stem: Budgeted manufacturing overhead is 30000 and the base is 6000 machine hours. What predetermined rate results?
B.explanation: 30000÷6000 = 5 per machine hour.
options: 0.20 per machine hour.
5000 per machine hour.
5 per machine hour.
6 per labor hour.

B.indicatorText: Adequately calculates rates for each element of cost using bases.
B.stem: A cost card gives materials 10, labor 6 and overhead 4 per unit. What is standard unit manufacturing cost?
B.explanation: 10+6+4 = 20 without duplicating labor.

B.indicatorText: Distinguishes introductory concepts of costs for continuous or departmental process.
B.stem: There are 100 units in process at 40% conversion. How much equivalent conversion work do they represent?
options: 100 equivalent units.
40 equivalent units.
250 equivalent units.
140 equivalent units.

B.indicatorText: Summarizes costs.
B.stem: Beginning work in process costs 500, added costs 3500 and ending work in process 600. What cost is transferred out under the case?

B.indicatorText: Comments about countable field processes of combined products, by-products and co-products.
B.stem: A cost is incurred after split-off exclusively to finish product A. How is it classified?
B.explanation: Its timing and traceability distinguish it from the common pre-split cost.
options: A joint cost incurred before separation.
A cost of every product in equal amounts by definition.
An owner distribution.
A separable cost of product A.

B.indicatorText: Applies methods to assign combined costs.
B.stem: Joint cost is 6000. Sales values at split-off are A 12000 and B 8000. What is allocated to B by relative sales value?

B.indicatorText: Differs among physical and mental load.
B.stem: Reconciling conflicting records while receiving frequent interruptions mainly increases which demand?
B.explanation: The task requires retaining and processing information while switching attention.
options: Only the weight of the keyboard.
Mental attention and decision-making demand.
Only the brightness of the building exterior.
No demand because the task is performed sitting down.

B.indicatorText: Describes consequences of physical and mental workload on people and productivity.
B.stem: Why can a faster pace fail to improve overall productivity?
B.explanation: Performance must include the quality and cost of completing the work.
options: Additional errors and rework can offset the apparent time saved.
Every faster task necessarily has better quality.
Rework never uses resources.
Output count always measures all consequences.

B.indicatorText: Identifies principles that regulate the auditor.
B.stem: An auditor lacks expertise for a specialized task. What reflects competence and due care?
B.explanation: The work requires capability and diligent performance.
options: Sign the conclusion first and learn later.
Obtain suitable expertise or support before undertaking work beyond capability.
Assume confidence is equivalent to competence.
Avoid documenting the knowledge gap.

B.indicatorText: Determines the means to achieve the internal control in corporate accounts.
B.stem: Which example is mainly a detective control?
B.explanation: The reconciliation compares records to detect discrepancies.
options: Blocking an unauthorized payment before release.
Requiring approval before a purchase.
An independent bank reconciliation identifying unexplained differences.
Restricting system access before use.

B.indicatorText: Interprets situations concerning the means to achieve a better internal control of the accounts of the company.
B.stem: A supplier bank-account change arrives by email. Which control addresses payment redirection risk?
B.explanation: Independent verification avoids relying solely on the potentially compromised request.
options: Verify the change using a previously trusted contact channel.
Reply only to the new address to ask if it is genuine.
Pay immediately because the message is urgent.
Skip verification if the invoice amount is small.

B.indicatorText: Mentions the projected profit and loss statement also the objectives of the projected profit and loss statement.
B.stem: What is a main purpose of a projected profit and loss statement?
B.explanation: The statement supports planning and comparison, not certainty.
options: Guarantee that every customer will pay on time.
Estimate future operating results from stated assumptions.
Replace the cash budget in all respects.
Record only past bank deposits.

B.indicatorText: Determines methods to project sales.
B.stem: A weighted forecast uses 0.6 for the latest sales of 200 and 0.4 for the previous sales of 150. What is the forecast?

C.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones relativas a las cuentas y sus componentes.
C.stem: ¿Qué movimiento aumenta normalmente una cuenta de ingresos?
C.explanation: Los ingresos tienen naturaleza acreedora.
options: Un débito.
Una anotación fuera del diario.
Un crédito.
Una reducción automática de pasivos.

C.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de transacciones contables en el libro diario.
C.stem: Se paga a un proveedor una deuda registrada por 450. ¿Qué cuenta se debita?
C.explanation: El débito reduce el pasivo que se está cancelando.
options: Ingreso por servicios.
Caja.
Cuentas por pagar.
Aportes del propietario.

C.indicatorText: Reconoce las NIIFs usadas en operaciones mercantiles de una empresa de servicios.
C.stem: ¿Qué información aportan las notas a los estados financieros?
C.explanation: Las cifras necesitan contexto para representar adecuadamente los hechos.
options: Políticas, estimaciones y explicaciones relevantes para interpretar cifras.
Solo publicidad comercial.
Una sustitución de todos los estados.
Garantía de que no existen riesgos.

C.indicatorText: Reconoce las NIIFs usadas en operaciones mercantiles de una empresa de servicios.
C.stem: Una empresa decide aplicar una norma de NIIF completas y otra de PYMES solo porque cada una produce más utilidad. ¿Qué falla?
C.explanation: La selección del marco no es una combinación oportunista de resultados.
options: Utiliza necesariamente una política permitida.
No mantiene un marco contable coherente y aplicable.
Está corrigiendo un error aritmético.
Mejora automáticamente comparabilidad.

C.indicatorText: Realiza cálculos sobre operaciones con mercancías y el cálculo del impuesto de ventas y la declaración respectiva.
C.stem: Débito fiscal 780 y crédito plenamente admisible 520, sin otros ajustes. ¿Cuál es el saldo por pagar?

C.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de ajuste, relacionados con los ingresos y gastos diferidos y acumulados.
C.stem: Un alquiler anticipado tiene saldo 1000 antes de ajustar y se consumieron 250. ¿Qué saldo del activo queda?
C.explanation: El consumo reduce el activo: 1000−250.

C.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de ajuste, relacionados con los ingresos y gastos diferidos y acumulados.
C.stem: ¿Qué caracteriza a un ingreso diferido cobrado por un servicio aún pendiente?
C.explanation: La entidad recibió recursos pero todavía debe cumplir el servicio.
options: Siempre es utilidad completa del día del cobro.
Es una cuenta de gasto.
No produce ningún registro porque aún no se trabaja.
Se mantiene como obligación hasta cumplir lo que permite reconocer ingreso.

C.indicatorText: Describe la importancia del marco conceptual de las NIIFs en las operaciones de una empresa comercial.
C.stem: ¿Por qué la importancia relativa no se decide solo con una cifra universal?
C.explanation: Magnitud y naturaleza se evalúan en las circunstancias de la entidad.
options: Porque cualquier error es siempre irrelevante.
Porque solo importa el saldo de caja.
Porque cada gerente puede ocultar lo que prefiera.
Porque también depende de la naturaleza y el contexto del hecho.

C.indicatorText: Aplica las NIIFs, en las operaciones y estados financieros para una empresa comercial.
C.stem: Una mercancía no vendida al cierre conserva costo recuperable. ¿Dónde se presenta normalmente?
C.explanation: La existencia no vendida mantiene su condición de activo.
options: Como inventario en el activo.
Como ingreso de ventas.
Como capital aportado.
Como pasivo por pagar aunque ya se pagó.

C.indicatorText: Identifica los alcances, etapas, consecuencias y señales de alerta de la legitimación de capitales.
C.stem: Una operación es inusual para el perfil del cliente. ¿Qué significa inicialmente?
C.explanation: La alerta inicia una revisión proporcional y documentada.
options: Que debe publicarse el nombre del cliente como culpable.
Que toda explicación del cliente es falsa por definición.
Que puede ignorarse si genera una comisión alta.
Que requiere análisis según el procedimiento, no que el delito esté probado.

C.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones relativas a la legitimación de capitales.
C.stem: ¿Cómo debe manejarse información sobre una operación que requiere revisión?
C.explanation: La información sensible debe limitarse a quienes intervienen legítimamente.
options: Por canales autorizados y con confidencialidad.
En redes sociales con nombres completos.
Por rumores entre clientes.
Sin conservar ningún soporte.

C.indicatorText: Contrasta las obligaciones de patronos y trabajadores ante la Caja Costarricense del Seguro Social (C.C.S.S). y el Código de Trabajo.
C.stem: Un trabajador entrega datos falsos para su identificación en la planilla. ¿Qué deber afecta?
C.explanation: Los datos correctos permiten atribuir cotizaciones y derechos.
options: Aumentar la publicidad del negocio.
Elegir el plan de ventas.
Suministrar información veraz necesaria para el registro.
Reemplazar al patrono como recaudador.

C.indicatorText: Contrasta las obligaciones de patronos y trabajadores ante la Caja Costarricense del Seguro Social (C.C.S.S). y el Código de Trabajo.
C.stem: Dos partes acuerdan no asegurar una relación laboral que legalmente debe asegurarse. ¿Qué conclusión es válida?
C.explanation: Los derechos y deberes imperativos no se anulan por comodidad de las partes.
options: El acuerdo privado siempre sustituye la ley.
La obligación desaparece si el salario es semanal.
El acuerdo no elimina por sí solo la obligación legal.
Solo importa que no quede por escrito.

C.indicatorText: Reconoce lo referente la normativa del Impuesto sobre las Ventas y el Impuesto sobre Bienes Muebles.
C.stem: ¿Qué institución administra el impuesto sobre bienes inmuebles dentro de su ámbito territorial?
C.explanation: La administración municipal se distingue de otros regímenes tributarios.
options: La empresa que vende combustible.
La municipalidad correspondiente.
La asociación de proveedores de software.
El banco elegido por el propietario como única autoridad tributaria.

C.indicatorText: Calcula la resolución de situaciones que involucren el cálculo y registro del impuesto sobre ventas y el Impuesto sobre Bienes Muebles.
C.stem: Se paga un impuesto del período por 700 que ya estaba reconocido como pasivo. ¿Qué asiento evita duplicar el gasto?
C.explanation: El pago cancela una obligación registrada previamente.
options: Débito a gasto y crédito a ingreso por 700.
Débito al impuesto por pagar y crédito a efectivo por 700.
Débito a efectivo y crédito a gasto por 700.
Crédito adicional al pasivo sin contrapartida.

C.indicatorText: Recognize appropriate habits to work with computers.
C.stem: A power cable crosses a busy walkway. What is the appropriate response?
C.explanation: A functioning device does not make its surroundings safe.
options: Route or secure it safely so it does not create a trip hazard.
Cover it with loose paper.
Ask everyone to remember to jump over it.
Leave it because the computer still works.

C.indicatorText: Apply hygiene and security habits when using a computer.
C.stem: A file from an unexpected sender asks the user to enable active content. What is the safer action?
C.explanation: The message and attachment must be evaluated before potentially unsafe execution.
options: Enable it immediately because it mentions accounting.
Verify the message through an approved channel and follow reporting procedures.
Forward it to all colleagues for testing.
Disable protection so it opens faster.

C.indicatorText: Define the concept and characteristic of viruses.
C.stem: A program secretly collects browser activity and sends it to another party. Which label describes its main purpose?
C.explanation: Its purpose is covert collection and disclosure of information.
options: Ransomware encrypting files for payment.
Spyware.
A worm classified by network replication.
A destructive wiper erasing stored files.

C.indicatorText: Differentiate characteristics of different anti virus.
C.stem: Why are detection updates important?
C.explanation: Updated detection is one layer within a broader security process.
options: They guarantee that no attack can ever succeed.
They replace all operating-system updates.
They can improve recognition of newly documented threats.
They remove the need to verify software sources.

C.indicatorText: Distinguishes characteristics, functions and services for different devices.
C.stem: Two cables have USB-C connectors. What should be checked before using one for an external display?
C.explanation: Connector shape alone does not establish video support.
options: Only that both connectors fit physically.
The supported capabilities of the cable, port and devices.
Only that the laptop battery can charge.
Only that the cable transfers a small text file.

C.indicatorText: Distinguishes characteristics, functions and services for different devices.
C.stem: A phone shares its cellular data connection with a laptop. Which function is being used?
C.explanation: The phone provides another device access through its available data connection.
options: Offline synchronization over a local folder.
A printer access queue.
A mobile hotspot or tethering.
Local screen rotation.

C.indicatorText: Differentiates the new theories used to manage the modern organizations.
C.stem: A firm hires a provider to operate payroll processing. What remains necessary?
C.explanation: Outsourcing changes delivery arrangements, not the need for control.
options: Assuming all accountability disappeared.
Giving the provider unrestricted access to every system.
Stopping all checks because the work is external.
Oversight of the service, data handling and contractual obligations.

C.indicatorText: Differentiates the new theories used to manage the modern organizations.
C.stem: Why does a systems approach examine several departments together?
C.explanation: End-to-end performance depends on interactions among activities.
options: Every department must perform the same task.
A local improvement may shift delays or costs elsewhere.
Only the largest department affects results.
Departmental boundaries prevent all interaction.

C.indicatorText: Defines marketing.
C.stem: A company advertises a service before checking whether the target group needs it. What should it investigate?
C.explanation: An offering must relate to a relevant market problem or desire.
options: Only a larger advertising font.
Only the number of employees.
Whether competitors use the same color.
The group’s needs and evidence of demand.

C.indicatorText: Recognizes variables of mixed market.
C.stem: An advertisement explains a service’s benefits to potential customers. Which P is most directly involved?
C.explanation: The decision concerns communication with the market.
options: Warehouse location only.
Product manufacturing only.
Payment collection only.
Promotion.

C.indicatorText: Describes the behavior of a professional at the table, as a host, or guest in a restaurant or at home.
C.stem: A confidential payroll issue arises in a crowded restaurant. What is the appropriate response?
C.explanation: A public location can expose sensitive information.
options: Read the figures quietly but within others’ hearing.
Show the spreadsheet to the whole table without authorization.
Move that discussion to a suitable private setting.
Assume the meal removes confidentiality obligations.

C.indicatorText: Defines compound interest components.
C.stem: What does compound interest add to later interest calculations?
C.explanation: Retained interest becomes part of the balance earning interest.
options: Only the original principal, with no accumulated interest.
Only future deposits not yet made.
Only service fees paid out of the account.
Previously earned interest that remains invested.

C.indicatorText: Calculates compound interest.
C.stem: An investment of 1000 compounds at 2% per quarter for four quarters. What is the future amount, rounded to cents?

C.indicatorText: Calculates factoring in managerial financing means.
C.stem: A factoring case advances 80% of invoices with a face value of $12,000. A fee of $240 is deducted from that advance. How much cash is received immediately?
C.explanation: Advance = 12,000 × 0.80 = 9,600. Immediate cash = 9,600 − 240 = 9,360. The unadvanced portion is not immediate cash.

C.indicatorText: Lists the concept and importance of accounts payable.
C.stem: What should happen when an already recorded supplier balance is paid?
C.explanation: Settlement cancels the obligation without duplicating the original transaction.
options: Recognize the purchase expense again.
Increase revenue from the supplier.
Reduce the payable and the cash balance.
Increase the payable by the payment.

C.indicatorText: Solves payable accounts transactions in foreign currencies and operations shown in financial statements with corresponding footnotes.
C.stem: A USD 1000 payable is carried at CRC 530000 and is settled at CRC 510 per USD. What difference arises on settlement?
C.explanation: Cash paid is 510000, below the liability of 530000 by 20000.
options: An exchange loss of CRC 20000.
A gain of CRC 510000.
An exchange gain of CRC 20000.
No difference under any circumstances.

C.indicatorText: Mentions about inventories according to company’s nature (activity).
C.stem: A dealership uses one vehicle for its own deliveries instead of holding it for sale. What determines its different classification?
C.explanation: Classification depends on the purpose and applicable recognition rules.
options: Its color compared with the vehicles for sale.
Its parking place alone.
Its use in operations rather than resale.
The fact that every vehicle must be inventory.

C.indicatorText: Determines reasons for adjusting entries.
C.stem: A count differs from the ledger. What should be done before assuming a cause?
C.explanation: Several causes can explain the difference.
options: Label the difference as theft immediately.
Investigate counts, documents, cutoff and relevant conditions.
Write a balancing entry without support.
Alter the count sheet to match the ledger.

C.indicatorText: Recognizes importance of property term, place and equipment.
C.stem: An asset costs 10000 and has estimated residual value 1000. What is its depreciable amount?
C.explanation: Depreciable amount = cost−residual value = 9000.

C.indicatorText: Answers cases of property, place and equipment and its presentation in the general balance.
C.stem: Equipment cost is 9000 and accumulated depreciation is 3500, with no impairment. What is the carrying amount?

C.indicatorText: Names accounts that make the patrimony.
C.stem: Does a retained earnings balance necessarily mean the same amount is held in cash?
C.explanation: Equity describes financing and residual interest, not a particular asset location.
options: Yes; it must match a dedicated bank deposit.
Yes; retained earnings is another name for currency.
No; retained earnings can never relate to past profit.
No; those resources may be invested in different assets.

C.indicatorText: Classifies patrimony accounts.
C.stem: How is an ordinary dividend distribution distinguished from an operating expense?
C.explanation: Owners receive a distribution in their ownership capacity.
options: It is a cost of selling goods in every case.
It is a distribution to owners that reduces equity.
It is a supplier payment for materials.
It is automatically revenue for the paying entity.

C.indicatorText: Mentions aspects about the savings and loan associations.
C.stem: Why should member savings and other contribution funds be recorded separately?
C.explanation: Different rights require appropriate classification and settlement.
options: Separate records make every fund tax-free.
Their ownership, withdrawal rights and treatment may differ.
Every contribution is always sales revenue.
All members necessarily have identical balances.

C.indicatorText: Names objectives of the working capital analysis and statement of change in the financial position based on cash.
C.stem: Why can positive profit coexist with low cash?
C.explanation: Accrual recognition and collection can occur in different periods.
options: Every profitable sale is necessarily collected immediately.
Depreciation automatically creates a cash deposit.
Profit and cash are always identical.
Some recognized revenue may still be uncollected.

C.indicatorText: Enumerates the financial control of the working capital.
C.stem: A major customer delays payment beyond the forecast date. What should treasury do?
C.explanation: A changed inflow assumption can affect the ability to meet commitments.
options: Leave the forecast unchanged because the sale was profitable.
Treat the delayed amount as cash already received.
Update the cash forecast and assess the resulting payment gap.
Delete the supplier due dates.

C.indicatorText: Lists objectives and importance of both statements for the companies.
C.stem: Equipment is acquired entirely by issuing a long-term note, with no cash paid. How is it treated in cash-flow totals?
C.explanation: The transaction affects assets and liabilities but has no current cash flow.
options: It is both a cash inflow and outflow despite no cash movement.
It is an operating cash receipt.
It is excluded from cash-flow totals and considered for separate noncash disclosure.
It is omitted from all accounting records.

C.indicatorText: Applies methods to develop the analysis of the working capital and statements of change in the financial position based on the working capital.
C.stem: Beginning cash is 200; operating cash inflow 150, investing outflow 100 and financing inflow 80. What is ending cash?

C.indicatorText: Recognizes the tools used to carry out financial analysis statements.
C.stem: Which tool compares selected financial figures through relationships such as current assets divided by current liabilities?
C.explanation: A ratio relates figures to address an analytical question.
options: Ratio analysis.
Only document alphabetization.
Only bank reconciliation.
Only chronological journal posting.

C.indicatorText: Interprets the results obtained from the financial ratios.
C.stem: Cost of goods sold is 12000. Beginning inventory is 5000 and ending inventory 7000; use their simple average. What is inventory turnover?
C.explanation: Average inventory = 6000; turnover = 12000÷6000 = 2.
options: 1.71 times.
2.4 times.
2 times.
0.5 times.

C.indicatorText: Recognizes concept of leaders, types of leaders and functions of leaders.
C.stem: What is needed when delegating a task?
C.explanation: Delegation works when people know what they can decide and what outcomes matter.
options: Responsibility with no access to information.
A guarantee that the manager has no remaining accountability.
A clear scope, appropriate authority and agreed follow-up.
Complete absence of expected results.

C.indicatorText: Recognizes the importance of administrative inventory systems in a company as in delay time, line, locations, suppliers and storage of raw material.
C.stem: For expiry-sensitive goods, which physical picking rule targets the earliest expiry date?
C.explanation: FEFO focuses on expiry rather than only receipt date.
options: Always pick the newest expiry first.
Always pick the most expensive item first.
First-expiring-first-out.
Pick without checking dates.

C.indicatorText: Recognizes the importance of administrative inventory systems in a company as in delay time, line, locations, suppliers and storage of raw material.
C.stem: A company orders again because on-hand stock is low but ignores a large order already in transit. What risk increases?
C.explanation: Outstanding orders must be considered in inventory position.
options: Automatic elimination of holding cost.
A guaranteed reduction in every lead time.
The disappearance of supplier obligations.
Duplicate replenishment and excess stock.

C.indicatorText: Adequately calculates rates for each element of cost using bases.
C.stem: Budgeted overhead is $36,000 and budgeted machine time is 9,000 hours. What predetermined overhead rate applies per machine hour?
C.explanation: Divide budgeted overhead by the stated activity base: 36,000/9,000 = 4 per machine hour.
options: $0.25 per machine hour.
$4 per machine hour.
$9 per machine hour.
$27,000 per machine hour.

C.indicatorText: Adequately calculates rates for each element of cost using bases.
C.stem: Actual production is 400 units and standard material use is 2 kg per unit. What material quantity is allowed for that output?

C.indicatorText: Distinguishes introductory concepts of costs for continuous or departmental process.
C.stem: Why may equivalent units for materials differ from those for conversion?
C.explanation: The timing of each element determines the work represented.
options: Materials and conversion can be added at different stages or rates.
Every physical unit must always have the same completion percentage for all elements.
Conversion never affects incomplete goods.
Equivalent units are another name for selling price.

C.indicatorText: Summarizes costs.
C.stem: Available costs are 9000. Transferred costs are 7600 and ending work in process 1400. What does the comparison show?
options: There is a missing cost of 1400.
Transferred costs must equal available costs alone.
The ending inventory must be recorded twice.
The assigned total reconciles to available costs.

C.indicatorText: Comments about countable field processes of combined products, by-products and co-products.
C.stem: What distinguishes a by-product in this introductory classification?
C.explanation: Economic significance, not size alone, guides the distinction.
options: It must be physically smaller in every case.
It must have no sale value.
Relatively minor economic importance compared with the main outputs.
It must be a defective main product.

C.indicatorText: Applies methods to assign combined costs.
C.stem: An output’s final sales value is 9000 and specified separable costs are 2000. What net amount is used in the stated NRV allocation base?

C.indicatorText: Differs among physical and mental load.
C.stem: Can one task involve both physical and mental workload?
C.explanation: For example, repetitive data entry can combine posture demands and sustained attention.
options: No; every task has exactly one type.
Only if no computer is used.
Yes; the two types can coexist.
Only if the task lasts less than a minute.

C.indicatorText: Describes consequences of physical and mental workload on people and productivity.
C.stem: Which action addresses an organizational source of overload?
C.explanation: Changing task conditions can reduce the mismatch between demands and resources.
options: Tell staff to ignore fatigue indefinitely.
Punish every report of difficulty.
Measure only attendance at the desk.
Clarify conflicting priorities and provide suitable resources.

C.indicatorText: Identifies principles that regulate the auditor.
C.stem: What does professional skepticism involve?
C.explanation: Skepticism supports balanced evaluation rather than blind trust or universal suspicion.
options: Assuming everyone is dishonest.
Questioning and critically assessing relevant evidence.
Accepting every management explanation without support.
Rejecting all documentary evidence automatically.

C.indicatorText: Determines the means to achieve the internal control in corporate accounts.
C.stem: Which is normally a permanent or real account?
C.explanation: The receivable carries its balance forward rather than closing as a period result account.
options: Sales revenue for the period.
Current-period advertising expense.
Accounts receivable.
The period’s wage expense.

C.indicatorText: Interprets situations concerning the means to achieve a better internal control of the accounts of the company.
C.stem: A former employee still has access to payroll after leaving. What should be corrected?
C.explanation: Access must follow current responsibilities and employment status.
options: Revoke the access and review relevant activity according to procedure.
Keep the account indefinitely for convenience.
Share the account among remaining staff.
Assume departure automatically disabled every system.

C.indicatorText: Mentions the projected profit and loss statement also the objectives of the projected profit and loss statement.
C.stem: Why should the projection show its key assumptions?
C.explanation: Transparent assumptions support review and scenario analysis.
options: Assumptions make actual results unnecessary.
Every assumption must be certain to be useful.
Users need to understand and test how the expected result was formed.
Only the final profit number has any meaning.

C.indicatorText: Determines methods to project sales.
C.stem: What does a seasonal sales pattern describe?
C.explanation: Seasonality is recurring variation, distinct from one-time events and long-term trend.
options: A recurring pattern associated with parts of a year or another defined cycle.
Any isolated unusually large sale.
A guarantee that every month has equal demand.
Only a permanent upward trend.

D.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones relativas a las cuentas y sus componentes.
D.stem: La propietaria aporta efectivo 100; después se paga una deuda ya registrada por 40. ¿Cuál es el cambio neto en activo, pasivo y patrimonio?
D.explanation: El aporte aumenta caja y patrimonio; pagar la deuda reduce caja y pasivo.
options: Activo +100, pasivo +40 y patrimonio +60.
Activo +60, pasivo −40 y patrimonio +100.
Activo −40, pasivo −40 y patrimonio sin cambio.
Activo +60, pasivo sin cambio y patrimonio +60.

D.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de transacciones contables en el libro diario.
D.stem: Un cliente entrega 600 por servicios que se prestarán el próximo mes. Aún no se ha satisfecho la obligación. ¿Qué registro inicial representa el hecho?
D.explanation: El cobro anticipado origina una obligación pendiente, no un servicio ya prestado.
options: Débito a efectivo y crédito inmediato a ingreso ganado.
Débito a gasto y crédito a efectivo.
Débito a efectivo y crédito a anticipo de clientes o pasivo contractual.
Débito a cuentas por pagar y crédito a capital.

D.indicatorText: Reconoce las NIIFs usadas en operaciones mercantiles de una empresa de servicios.
D.stem: Una agencia terminó el servicio y tiene derecho a cobrar 1200, aunque el cliente pagará después. El caso satisface los requisitos de reconocimiento. ¿Qué efecto corresponde?
D.explanation: Bajo los supuestos, el devengo reconoce el servicio satisfecho y el derecho de cobro.
options: Reconocer ingreso y cuenta por cobrar.
Esperar siempre hasta cobrar para reconocer ingreso.
Reconocer únicamente un anticipo del cliente.
Registrar gasto por 1200.

D.indicatorText: Reconoce las NIIFs usadas en operaciones mercantiles de una empresa de servicios.
D.stem: Una empresa de capacitación posee un edificio de uso propio y también vende manuales. ¿Por qué no aplica el mismo tratamiento a ambos activos?
D.explanation: Un activo de uso prolongado se distingue de inventario mantenido para venta.
options: Porque solo los manuales tienen valor.
Porque todo activo de servicios es intangible.
Su función y naturaleza llevan a normas y mediciones distintas.
Porque el edificio siempre se reconoce como ingreso.

D.indicatorText: Realiza cálculos sobre operaciones con mercancías y el cálculo del impuesto de ventas y la declaración respectiva.
D.stem: Una venta con base 1500 y tarifa del caso 13 % se revierte íntegramente mediante documento válido dentro del período. ¿Cuánto disminuye su débito fiscal?
D.explanation: La reversión del impuesto es 1500×0,13 = 195.

D.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de ajuste, relacionados con los ingresos y gastos diferidos y acumulados.
D.stem: El 1 de octubre se pagó una cobertura uniforme de seis meses por 1800, registrada como activo. Al 31 de diciembre no hubo ajustes previos. ¿Qué gasto corresponde reconocer?
D.explanation: Octubre, noviembre y diciembre representan tres de seis meses: 1800×3÷6.

D.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones de ajuste, relacionados con los ingresos y gastos diferidos y acumulados.
D.stem: Un pasivo por anticipos era 2400; durante el período se cumplió y ganó el 75 % del servicio. ¿Cuál es el pasivo final?
D.explanation: La parte pendiente es 25 % de 2400 = 600.

D.indicatorText: Describe la importancia del marco conceptual de las NIIFs en las operaciones de una empresa comercial.
D.stem: La gerencia elimina una nota relevante porque el asunto es complejo. ¿Qué mejora la comprensibilidad sin sacrificar información?
D.explanation: La claridad organiza información relevante; no justifica omitirla.
options: Explicarlo con claridad y contexto conservando lo necesario.
Suprimir toda cifra relacionada.
Cambiar el hecho económico por uno más simple.
Presentar solo noticias favorables.

D.indicatorText: Aplica las NIIFs, en las operaciones y estados financieros para una empresa comercial.
D.stem: Una compra incluye inventario 4000 y publicidad posterior 600 facturados juntos. No hay impuestos. ¿Qué debe evitarse?
D.explanation: Compartir factura no convierte todos los conceptos en costo del inventario.
options: Separar conceptos por su naturaleza.
Capitalizar automáticamente los 4600 como inventario.
Revisar el soporte.
Reconocer publicidad como gasto cuando corresponde.

D.indicatorText: Identifica los alcances, etapas, consecuencias y señales de alerta de la legitimación de capitales.
D.stem: Una empresa descarta una alerta porque no observa las tres etapas del modelo en orden. ¿Qué error comete?
D.explanation: Las etapas son una herramienta conceptual; pueden superponerse o no ser observables en la información disponible.
options: Exige una secuencia didáctica rígida como condición para analizar el riesgo.
Aplica correctamente una prueba legal universal de inocencia.
Demuestra que toda operación aislada es irrelevante.
Confunde una alerta con un impuesto aduanero.

D.indicatorText: Resuelve situaciones relativas a la legitimación de capitales.
D.stem: Un supervisor propone cambiar la descripción de un depósito inusual para que coincida con el giro, sin soporte. ¿Qué respuesta mantiene integridad?
D.explanation: Modificar la narrativa sin evidencia oculta el riesgo y distorsiona la contabilidad.
options: Conservar los hechos y elevar la inconsistencia al canal competente.
Aceptar porque el asiento queda cuadrado.
Fraccionar el depósito en ventas pequeñas.
Eliminar el comprobante original.

D.indicatorText: Contrasta las obligaciones de patronos y trabajadores ante la Caja Costarricense del Seguro Social (C.C.S.S). y el Código de Trabajo.
D.stem: Un auxiliar retuvo correctamente una cuota, pero el patrono destinó el dinero a comprar inventario y omitió enterarlo. ¿Qué control falló?
D.explanation: Una retención correcta no basta si no se cumple el destino y pago exigibles.
options: El reconocimiento de una venta al trabajador.
La eliminación del salario bruto.
El cálculo del valor residual de maquinaria.
Cumplir y conciliar la obligación generada por la retención.

D.indicatorText: Contrasta las obligaciones de patronos y trabajadores ante la Caja Costarricense del Seguro Social (C.C.S.S). y el Código de Trabajo.
D.stem: Una jefatura ordena cambiar horas trabajadas para ocultar una obligación salarial. ¿Qué respuesta es adecuada?
D.explanation: La subordinación laboral no autoriza falsificación de información.
options: Modificar las horas porque toda orden es legítima.
Eliminar comprobantes para evitar diferencias.
Conservar registros veraces y usar el canal de revisión o denuncia pertinente.
Pedir al trabajador que firme un dato falso.

D.indicatorText: Reconoce lo referente la normativa del Impuesto sobre las Ventas y el Impuesto sobre Bienes Muebles.
D.stem: Una hoja calcula el tributo de un inmueble usando una tasa copiada de una factura comercial. ¿Qué dato debe verificarse primero?
D.explanation: Una tarifa de IVA no se traslada a un impuesto de propiedad por coincidencia de formato.
options: La norma, base y tarifa del tributo inmobiliario aplicable.
Solo el nombre del archivo.
Si la factura tenía un logotipo.
Que ambas cifras sean positivas.

D.indicatorText: Calcula la resolución de situaciones que involucren el cálculo y registro del impuesto sobre ventas y el Impuesto sobre Bienes Muebles.
D.stem: Un precio final de 6780 incluye IVA del 13 %. ¿Cuánto corresponde al impuesto?

D.indicatorText: Recognize appropriate habits to work with computers.
D.stem: A worker takes a screen break but spends it hunched over a phone. What remains unresolved?
D.explanation: Changing devices does not necessarily change the exposure that caused strain.
options: The break guarantees full recovery.
Phone use eliminates all repetitive movement.
The workstation no longer needs review.
The same visual and postural demands may continue.

D.indicatorText: Apply hygiene and security habits when using a computer.
D.stem: A suspected infection appears on a shared computer. A worker wants to delete logs before reporting it. What should be done?
D.explanation: Uncontrolled deletion can hinder investigation and recovery.
options: Delete all traces so nobody is concerned.
Follow the incident procedure and preserve relevant evidence.
Move the suspicious file to another workstation and run it.
Share the account password to simplify investigation.

D.indicatorText: Define the concept and characteristic of viruses.
D.stem: A malicious spreadsheet macro executes when the infected workbook is opened with macros enabled and infects other workbooks. What supports classifying it as a virus?
D.explanation: The described host-based replication matters, not ordinary spreadsheet use.
options: The spreadsheet contains any arithmetic formula.
The file is stored in a folder.
Replication through infected host documents and their execution.
The monitor displays rows and columns.

D.indicatorText: Differentiate characteristics of different anti virus.
D.stem: A scan finds nothing, but suspicious outbound activity continues. What is the sound conclusion?
D.explanation: Detection has limits, and other evidence still matters.
options: Every network event must be harmless.
The logs should be deleted because the scan was clean.
All other controls can be removed.
The clean scan does not rule out every threat; investigate the remaining evidence.

D.indicatorText: Distinguishes characteristics, functions and services for different devices.
D.stem: Office computers can print locally but cannot reach a remote accounting server after the provider link fails. What does this indicate?
D.explanation: Local communication and remote connectivity depend on different paths.
options: Every local switch has necessarily failed.
Printing proves the remote server is reachable.
The printer has become the Internet provider.
Local services can remain available while the external path is unavailable.

D.indicatorText: Distinguishes characteristics, functions and services for different devices.
D.stem: A laptop charges through a port but does not send video through the connected adapter. What should be verified?
